svg.text: at 20 °C. Shrink goes on the CAVITY, not here
slot 6.09 deep from the moulding face
cut on the cross centre-line, so the slot reads full depth
cut on the cable centre-line -- the FFC exit is
0.50 wide at the seat floor and 3.50 at z = 0
section at z = 0.30, just above the lead-in chamfer
5.20 gap, 0.30 deep, 0.80 min to the edge
looking down +Z, as V3. Thin outline
= the face the stamp is cut into.
looking up -Z, as V4. Same stamp, same depth,
TURNED 180° -- not mirrored. It reads normally
when the part is flipped over front-to-back.
1. CRITICAL MX slot 4.05 x 1.10 ±0.03, R0.30 corner
fillets (V7). Gauge against a real MX switch stem, not by
CMM alone. Our slot is deliberately TIGHTER than Cherry's
published keycap slot; the four relief bulges are what
make that work. Verify on a moulded first article.
2. CRITICAL The transparent relegendable cap is an
off-the-shelf POS part, so that mating dimension is a
hard datum set by a supplier we do not control. Confirm
3. Draft, measured off the model: outer body 11.6°,
inside pocket 18.4°. ZERO DRAFT on the display seat (12.2
x 12.1 x 1.1 deep) and on its cable relief (V6) --
confirm release at first article rather than meeting it
4. Slot draft 0.08° on the flats, 0.31° at the arm tips,
opening downward: the core pin withdraws the right way,
but with very little relief. Polish along the arms. The
slot runs from the moulding face to z = 5.83 -- through
the boss and on into the cap floor (V5).
5. The inner chamfer in V4 (33.0°) is switch-body
clearance, not cosmetic -- it is what stops the cap
fouling a bulky switch. Do not flatten it to simplify the
6. The three 0.40 x 3.00 x 0.30 tabs standing 0.20 proud
(+Y and ±X, V3) are a FUNCTIONAL feature: they are what
makes the clear keycap click on properly. They are NOT a
3D-printing artefact and must NOT be removed.
7. Stamp "β S" = revision + profile, 0.30 deep, zero
draft, in TWO places: the display-seat floor (V8) and the
pocket ceiling (V9). The second is TURNED 180°, not
mirrored -- it reads normally when the part is flipped
over front-to-back. Drawn in V9; do not infer it.
Revision character is U+03B2 GREEK SMALL LETTER BETA --
the moulded part is deliberately β where the 3D-printed
prototypes are α, so the two are told apart by eye. Carry
it on a REPLACEABLE INSERT in the cavity rather than cut
into the block: a revision change is then a plug swap,
not a tool edit. Font Noto Sans Bold, outlines in the
8. The slot lead-in opens to 4.61 x 4.61 at z = 0 over
0.30 mm (~46°). Cherry publishes no lead-in dimension, so
this one is ours; keep it, it is what lets the cap start
9. GATE AND EJECTORS are the moulder's choice, but they
must NOT land on the MX slot or its lead-in, the display
seat floor or cable relief, the three click tabs, or the
moulding face (z = 0). A side wall (±X) clear of the tabs
is the obvious place, feeding toward the stem boss -- the
thickest section. The 3D-printed prototypes were sprued
from Ø1.5 runners on that same wall, so it already
tolerates a witness mark. Mark the positions chosen on
the tooling drawing and send it back.
10. Surface: tool polish on the slot and the stem bore;
the outer faces may carry the standard texture. No flash
permitted on the slot, the tabs or the seat floor.
